content.title: What are Comparable & Comparator?
content.description: Comparable and Comparator are interfaces used to define the ordering of objects in Java. Comparable provides the natural ordering of objects, while Comparator allows custom sorting based on different criteria.

content.content: Sorting is a common requirement in Java applications. The Comparable interface is implemented inside a class to define its default sorting order. The Comparator interface is implemented separately and allows multiple custom sorting strategies without modifying the original class.

content.title: Why Learn Comparable & Comparator?
content.content: These interfaces are essential for sorting collections, implementing custom ordering, and solving many coding interview problems involving objects.
The Comparable interface belongs to the java.lang package and contains a single method, compareTo(). It defines the natural ordering of objects.

content.title: Comparable Example
Key Idea
content.description: A class can implement Comparable only once because it defines a single natural ordering.

content.content: The Comparator interface belongs to the java.util package and provides the compare() method. It allows multiple custom sorting strategies without changing the original class.

content.title: Comparator Example
content.code:
Comparator<Student> byMarks = (s1, s2) -> s1.marks - s2.marks;
Collections.sort(studentList, byMarks);

content.title: Flexibility
content.content: A class can have multiple Comparator implementations for different sorting requirements, such as sorting by name, age, salary, or marks.

content.title: Sorting by Name
content.code:
Comparator<Student> byName = (s1, s2) -> s1.name.compareTo(s2.name);
Collections.sort(studentList, byName);

items.answer: Sort students by marks, roll number, or name.

items.question: Employee Records
items.answer: Sort employees by salary, department, or experience.

items.question: E-commerce
items.answer: Sort products by price, rating, or popularity.

items.question: Library Systems
items.answer: Sort books by title, author, or publication year.

content.title: Ranking Students
content.content: Imagine a school ranking students. If the default ranking is based on marks, it is like Comparable. If teachers sometimes rank students by attendance, sports, or behavior, those are different Comparators.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Comparable and Comparator are among the most frequently asked Java interview topics. Interviewers often ask about compareTo(), compare(), lambda expressions, sorting custom objects, and differences between natural and custom ordering.

items.question: Can a class implement multiple Comparable interfaces?
items.answer: No. A class can define only one natural ordering using Comparable.

items.question: Should Comparator modify the original class?
items.answer: No. Comparator is implemented separately to keep the original class unchanged.

items.question: Can compareTo() return only -1, 0, or 1?
items.answer: No. It can return any negative, zero, or positive integer.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use Comparable for default sorting built into a class and Comparator when different custom sorting strategies are required.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Comparator is commonly implemented using lambda expressions.

content.question: Which interface defines the natural ordering of objects?
Which method belongs to the Comparator interface?
When should Comparator be preferred over Comparable?
options: When only one default sorting order is needed
When multiple custom sorting strategies are required
content.answer: When multiple custom sorting strategies are required
